grading: Each eval says how it is graded. "human" means somebody reads the transcript and judges it; these are about drawing quality and layout, which no script can score. A path names a check script that runs in `bun run test` and asserts the objective part of the eval outright, leaving the transcript to answer only whether the agent chose the right path.

evals.prompt: Using only the CLI, with ARCHBOARD_VAULT pointing at /tmp/eval-vault (assume /tmp/eval-vault/.obsidian exists): draw the payments architecture as it stands today on a board named `payments` at service level. It is three things in a row: 'API Gateway' calls 'Orders Service', which reads and writes 'Orders Postgres'. Promote each one (gateway, service, datastore) and save the board. Now I want to look at a proposal called option-a that puts a read cache, 'Orders Cache', beside Orders Service, written to by Orders Service. Leave `payments` itself exactly as it is. When the proposal is drawn, show me what it changes and nothing else.
evals.expected_output: The variant was branched from the source with `board save --board payments --variant option-a`, and the only edits made on `payments@option-a` were the added 'Orders Cache' node and the one arrow into it. `compare payments payments@option-a` then reports `summary.comparable` true, `sharedNodes` 3, `nodesAdded` 1, `nodesRemoved` 0, `edgesAdded` 1, `edgesRemoved` 0, `edgesUnchanged` 2, with `nodes.added` naming only 'Orders Cache' and `edges.unchanged` holding 'API Gateway' to 'Orders Service' and 'Orders Service' to 'Orders Postgres'. The narration is the one added cache and its one edge. FAILS if `payments@option-a` was drawn on a fresh board instead of branched: that gives `sharedNodes` below 3 and `nodesRemoved` above 0, up to `comparable` false with everything removed and everything added, because `compare` joins on node identity and independently drawn boards share none. Reporting the `variantAnomaly` field on the copied nodes as an architectural difference is also wrong; it is the branch's bookkeeping, not a change to the design. The numbers are asserted outright by scripts/check-branch-compare.mjs on the same fixture, so what this eval grades is the choice: did the agent branch the board it was given, or draw the proposal again from scratch.

evals.prompt: Using only the CLI, draw the public edge of our system on a board named `edge` at system level: users hit a CDN, the CDN goes to a load balancer, the load balancer goes to a 'Web' service, and Web publishes onto a message queue. Before you draw anything, tell me what ready-made shapes are already there, and use one wherever it fits rather than drawing another box.
evals.expected_output: `library list --text` ran before any element was created, and the answer names what is in the palette (111 stencils across seven source libraries). The recognisable furniture came from the library via `library insert`, not from hand-drawn rectangles: a users stencil, 'CDN', 'Load balancer' and 'Message queue' all exist. 'Load balancer' and 'Users' are each a name two libraries use, so an insert without `--source` is refused with both candidates named and the retry passes `--source` or `--id`; that refusal is the expected path, not an error to work around. Placed elements carry `customData.library` recording the stencil they came from. The 'Web' service stayed a labelled rectangle, which is the right shape for a service box. FAILS if the whole diagram is plain rectangles, or if the library was only listed after the drawing was already done.

evals.prompt: Using only the CLI, with ARCHBOARD_VAULT pointing at /tmp/eval-vault (assume /tmp/eval-vault/.obsidian exists) and one pane open in the browser: draw the payments architecture as it stands on a board named `payments` at service level, three things in a row: 'API Gateway' calls 'Orders Service', which reads and writes 'Orders Postgres'. Promote each one and save. Then branch it into a proposal called option-a that adds a read cache, 'Orders Cache', written to by Orders Service, and put the proposal up beside the current architecture so I can see both at once. Draw the cache on the proposal, promote and save it, show me a picture of the proposal, and tell me what it changes. I am reading `payments` while you work, so leave it where it is.
evals.expected_output: Both boards end up on screen at once, and `payments` is still in the pane it started in. The proposal reached the screen through `pane open --board payments@option-a`, which makes a second pane and cannot be aimed at an existing one. Every write after that named the board it meant (`--board payments@option-a`), and the picture named the pane it meant (`screenshot --pane right`). `compare payments payments@option-a` reports one node added and nothing removed. FAILS if the branch was put up with `board open payments@option-a`: with one pane on screen that needs no `--pane`, so it is accepted, and it re-points the pane the human is reading, so the source goes off screen and the request to leave it alone is broken without anything reporting an error. Also FAILS if the agent expects `board save --board payments --variant option-a` to have moved anything, or repairs a move it did not make: a save writes a file and moves no pane (ADR 0012), so `saveKind` is `branch` and `panes.moved` is empty, and putting the branch on screen is a separate act. The pane state and the compare numbers are asserted outright by scripts/check-side-by-side.mjs on the same trace, so what this eval grades is the choice: did the agent make a pane for the proposal, or reuse the one it had?
